title: Ampleness detected by a fibrewise nonempty affine section locus on a smooth group
statement: Let $T$ be an affine locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth] whose local rings are integrally closed domains [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $p:G\to T$ be a smooth separated morphism of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], separated meaning that the diagonal is a closed immersion, and let $G$ be a group scheme over $T$: there are $T$-morphisms $m:G\times_TG\to G$, $i:G\to G$ and $e:T\to G$ satisfying the associativity, unit and inverse identities, equivalently $T'\mapsto G(T')=\operatorname{Hom}_T(T',G)$ takes values in groups (the relative form of [def-sc-group-scheme], whose base is a field). Assume that for every $t\in T$ the fibre $G_t=G\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-residue-field] is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_G$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], let $n\geq1$, and let $\sigma\in\Gamma(G,L^{\otimes n})$. Write $G_\sigma$ for the open where the residue-field value of $\sigma$ is nonzero [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. If $G_\sigma$ is affine and its intersection with every fibre of $p$ is nonempty, then $L$ is ample on $G$ in the absolute sense [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Neither commutativity nor properness of $G$, nor any symmetry or rigidification of $L$, is assumed. A single supplied section, rather than a pre-existing affine cover by section loci, is the hypothesis.

source.place: Guo, Proposition 5.9, final assertion, printed pp.13--14, and Corollary 6.6(ii), printed p.16 (Raynaud VI, Theorem 2.1), applied to the left translation action of G on itself. Some positive tensor power satisfies the theorem of the square; the section criterion then detects ampleness. Read online in the March 31, 2026 version; local copy WANTED. This is the locally Noetherian specialization, also for a normal affine base with finitely many disjoint integral components.

proof.text: Finite presentation gives quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of $G\to T$ by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Apply [lem-sfb-normal-group-square-power] to the supplied group and line: $T$ is affine, locally Noetherian and normal by the stated local-ring hypothesis; $G\to T$ is smooth separated of finite presentation with connected fibres. Obtain $r\geq1$ for which $A=L^{\otimes r}$ satisfies the square condition for left multiplication.

source.place: Proposition 5.9, final assertion; finite-component specialization isolated in the cited node

proof.text: Set $v=\sigma^{\otimes r}\in\Gamma(G,A^{\otimes n})$, using the reassociation $A^{\otimes n}\cong L^{\otimes nr}$. In a local frame, if $\sigma$ is represented by $f$, then $v$ is represented by $f^r$. At every residue field $f^r\ne0$ if and only if $f\ne0$, so $G_v=G_\sigma=:V$. Thus $V$ is affine and $V\to T$ is surjective by the hypothesis on every fibre. These are precisely the section loci of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].

By [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change], the projection $\pi:G\times_TV\to G$ is surjective, since it is the base change of $V\to T$. The maps $F(g,u)=(gu,u)$ and $F^{-1}(x,u)=(xu^{-1},u)$ are inverse $T$-morphisms of $G\times_TV$, by the group identities. Consequently multiplication $a:G\times_TV\to G$ equals $\pi\circ F$ and is surjective. If $U$ is the union of the affine section loci of positive powers of $A$, then $V=G_v\subseteq U$, so $G\times_TU\to G$ is surjective as well.

source.place: Corollary 6.5 orbit-cover hypothesis, explicit left-action computation

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-square-action-affine-orbit-criterion] with $S=T$, $H=X=G$, multiplication as action, and $M=A$. The square condition is Step 1, and Step 3 verifies the orbit-cover hypothesis; the two structure morphisms are the given separated finitely presented morphism. Thus $A$ is ample. For every $x\in G$, its ampleness supplies $k\geq1$ and $w\in\Gamma(G,A^{\otimes k})$ with $x\in G_w$ affine. Regard $w$ as a section of $L^{\otimes rk}$ by reassociating tensor factors. Its residue value and its locus are unchanged, and $rk\geq1$. Together with the quasi-compactness included in the ampleness of $A$, this proves ampleness of $L$ directly by [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].

source.place: Corollary 6.5; equivalently Corollary 6.6(ii); reflection of ampleness along a positive tensor power is the defining affine-locus criterion

proof_origin.place: Assembly following Guo Proposition 5.9 and Corollary 6.5, read online in the March 31, 2026 version. Local source WANTED. Explicit multiplication/projection argument replaces the maximal-fibre-point formulation of Corollary 6.6(ii).

The disconnected normal Noetherian base is handled with finitely many integral components, a common multiple of the exponents and the line N glued over each component of B. (3) lem-sfb-square-action-affine-orbit-criterion specializes Cor 6.5: smooth implies flat, finitely presented and universally open; affine X_s are quasi-affine, so the smaller union U still gives the cover; over an affine base, S-ample is absolute ample. (5) My DAG-wide search (theorem of the square, Picard-admissible, Raynaud, orbit+ample) found only commutative/semiabelian cubical nodes, so there are no duplicates.
